summary: FIRE ATLAS is a pre-flight fire check for any habitat atmosphere. We harvested all 25 combustion-related investigations in NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics database, normalized 22 experimental tables into 1,719 traceable tests, and placed them on one interactive atlas of oxygen and pressure next to real and planned crew habitats. The atlas exposes a gap that matters for Artemis: every solid-material test in PSI — 263 fabrics and plastics — was run at 22.2 % O₂ or less, while planned lunar habitats will use at least 30 % O₂. Inside that envelope there are zero solid tests. An SI layer writes fire-risk briefings for any habitat or plain-English question, but deterministic code computes every fact and a verifier checks every citation and number against the data; any point opens the original NASA row. Engineers also get gravity bounds (1 g vs microgravity), a material readiness matrix, investigation comparisons, and a citable dataset export.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

FIRE ATLAS is a pre-flight fire check for any habitat atmosphere. It turns NASA's microgravity combustion results into one view an engineer can act on:

1. Combustion atlas – 1,719 NASA PSI tests plotted by O2 concentration and pressure, colored by outcome (burned, self-extinguished, no ignition, unknown) and shaped by fuel phase (solid, droplet, gas). Curves of constant O2 partial pressure show that the Moon base (34 % O2 at 8.2 psi) has almost Earth's partial pressure but 63 % more oxygen by fraction. A 3D view shows tests per condition as towers next to the lunar habitat envelope.

2. Habitat check & SI briefing – choose a habitat (Earth, ISS, spacesuit, Moon base, Apollo 1) or type a question such as "Would Nomex burn in a lunar rover?". The SI returns a short briefing, evidence gaps and the next tests to run. Every sentence carries citations and every number is verified.

3. Original NASA record – any test opens the exact, unmodified row of NASA's CSV with the columns we used highlighted, plus DOI and PSI links.

4. Insights – gravity bounds from SAFFIRE-II (same samples at 1 g and in microgravity) and a material readiness matrix (6 materials with microgravity burn data, none tested at 30 % O2 or more).

5. Compare & export – all 25 investigations side by side with a hardware x fuel-phase matrix (CIR + ACME, CIR + MDCA, MSG + SPICE, Saffire), and filtered CSV/JSON export with provenance columns for modeling.

KEY FINDING

Every solid-material test in PSI (263 fabrics and plastics) was run at 22.2 % O2 or less, while planned lunar habitats will use at least 30 % O2. Inside that envelope there are zero solid-material tests.

HOW IT WORKS

A Python pipeline harvests PSI through its public API, normalizes 22 heterogeneous tables (unit conversion, O2 semantics for normal vs inverse flames, measured vs assumed values) and computes source-backed facts. A validation script re-checks every point against its raw NASA row. The web app runs on Vercel; serverless functions build an evidence pack of the nearest real tests, call free-tier SI models, and verify the answer before showing it. Deterministic code computes the facts – the SI only explains them. If no SI provider responds, a computed, fully cited briefing is shown instead.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Lunar habitats and pressurized rovers will use oxygen-enriched, reduced-pressure air to shorten spacesuit pre-breathing, and flammability rises with oxygen concentration. FIRE ATLAS makes the evidence gap obvious, quantifies it, and points to the experiments (e.g. for LUCI and FM2) that would close it. The same view applies on Earth to oxygen-enriched hospital rooms and home-oxygen therapy. The cleaned, provenance-tagged dataset is a ready training set for flammability models.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Instead of a chatbot over documents, we built a map where the gap is visible at a glance: a 3D landing shows a spherical microgravity flame whose 1,719 particles (the real tests) morph into the atlas. The SI is "receipts first": a judge can click any claim and see NASA's original row.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Trust and validity (no invented numbers; missing values stay empty and are flagged; assumed pressures are labeled), security (API keys server-side only, input range checks, rate limiting, prompt-injection tested), accessibility for non-experts, and zero cost (free-tier models, free hosting, open NASA data).

HONEST LIMITATIONS

PSI has no partial-gravity data yet; solid-test cabin pressures were not recorded (assumed and flagged); outcome shares are descriptive, not risk probabilities; SI briefings are decision support, not certification.

TOOLS AND LANGUAGES

Python (requests, pandas, openpyxl), TypeScript, React, Vite, Plotly.js, Three.js (react-three-fiber), Vercel serverless functions, Google Gemini and Groq APIs, Playwright for end-to-end tests, Remotion and FFmpeg for the demo video.

Code: https://github.com/zaindadabhoy/fire-atlas
